newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Nemtsov accepts post of first deputy PM - Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Nemtsov accepts post of first deputy PM - Kremlin.

text.p: Boris Nemtsov, the liberal governor of the Nizhny Novgorod region, has accepted President Boris Yeltsin's offer to become a first deputy prime minister in the new Russian government, the Kremlin said on Monday.
"Yes, we have such information," a presidential spokesman said. Nemtsov will be the second man in the government to hold this position, along with reformer Anatoly Chubais.

Yeltsin, who has pledged a sweeping government reshuffle, had previously appointed Chubais, his reformist chief of staff, to the cabinet with a pledge to make him the only first deputy to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
But he changed his mind surprisingly on Monday and offered Nemtsov, a 37-year-old reformer, the chance to become another first deputy premier.
Interfax news agency said Nemtsov would be responsible for the government's social programmes, handling natural monopolies and running uneasy relations with powerful regional authorities.
Yeltsin was due to meet Chernomyrdin and Chubais later on Tuesday to discuss the government line-up and structure.
